clue.text: My French speaking lady covering payment, with Heather in this mood

parts.note: mon is French for my

indicators.note: speaking signals that the next words are to be said out loud, giving a near-twin in sound

parts.note: a lady is a dame and a covering is an awning, together sounding like the weekday start
a fee is a payment
ling is another name for heather

explanation.surface: A Frenchman describes a lady and her Heather friend sunk in a gloomy mood, with a bill to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking' says DAME AWNING aloud, which sounds like DAY MORNING. Heather is LING, a common moorland plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the familiar reluctant, low spirits at the start of a working week, so it is a mood.

clue.text: Flower unknown among old English, yet timeless

indicators.note: among puts the unknown letter between the letters for old English

parts.note: X is the classic algebraic unknown

indicators.note: timeless asks for the word yet without its T, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A flower described in old English that is somehow outside time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' removes T (time) from YET, leaving YE.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye daisy is a common white wild flower of meadows.

clue.text: Mother's restraint

definitions.meaning: the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: A mother showing restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeder calls a foal's mother its dam, and a barrier holding back a river is also one.

clue.text: Jaguar perhaps to be buttressed with Chinese cash in part of Mexico

indicators.note: buttressed with means supported on both sides, so the money word flanks the animal

parts.note: the yuan is the Chinese currency
a jaguar is an example of a big cat

explanation.surface: A Jaguar car propped up by Chinese investment in a Mexican region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaguar' suggests the car, but here it is the big cat, and 'buttressed with' means the Chinese money supports it on both sides.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yucatan peninsula is a region in south-eastern Mexico.

clue.text: Actor's extremely involved in part right away

indicators.note: involved in places the word for extremely inside the trimmed word for part
right away tells you to take R, short for right, out of the word for part

parts.note: a part in a play is a role
too means extremely or excessively

explanation.surface: An actor gets thoroughly wrapped up in a role, ignoring everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' removes R, leaving OLE, and 'involved in' puts the word for extremely inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter O'Toole was the Irish star of Lawrence of Arabia, a famous film actor; the 's is read as 'is'.

clue.text: Old court performer's conjuring an asset

indicators.note: conjuring suggests a magician's trick, turning these letters into something new

explanation.surface: A veteran entertainer turns a skill into a valuable asset through a magic act.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'court' is a tennis court: Ilie Nastase was a Romanian tennis champion of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilie Nastase played top-level tennis decades ago, so he is a former performer on the court.

clue.text: Sceptic about Nobel I tentatively put "no way"

indicators.note: about has the words for no way wrapped round the rearranged letters

parts.note: never is an emphatic no way

indicators.note: something tentatively put is placed loosely and uncertainly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doubter hesitantly dismisses the Nobel prize with a flat no way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tentatively put' rearranges NOBEL I into ONBELI, which 'about' places inside the word for no way, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic doubts claims, just as an unbeliever rejects faith.

clue.text: To a degree, product's not at first made into sheets

parts.note: BEd is the Bachelor of Education degree
a line is a range of goods, a product line

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word not

explanation.surface: A product that has been partly developed is turned into sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degree' is BEd (Bachelor of Education); 'at first' keeps only N from 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets and pillowcases are what make up the cloth covering of a bed.

clue.text: Vary hairstyle

definitions.meaning: short for permutate, to vary the selection of combinations as in football pools
a set of waves or curls put into hair chemically

explanation.surface: Change your hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: On the football pools you perm, choosing combinations, and a salon perm is a lasting curl.

clue.text: One leaves Miss Francis to drape Miss Lane in jewellery

indicators.note: to drape has the trimmed singer's name wrapped round the second woman
leaves means the letter for one departs from the name

parts.note: Connie Francis was an American pop singer
I is the Roman numeral for one
Lois Lane is Superman's girlfriend

explanation.surface: One woman walks out, leaving Connie Francis to dress Lois Lane in jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' drops I (one) from the singer's name, giving CONNE; 'to drape' wraps it round Superman's girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloisonne is enamel work set in metal cells, used for decorative ornaments and brooches.

clue.text: Deprived official trapped in gamble

indicators.note: trapped in puts the official inside the wager word

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
a ref is a referee, a sports official

explanation.surface: A referee caught betting is left with nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means having lost something, so it is a synonym for deprived.

clue.text: "Amplification" from angler meant touch of embarrassment — for a change!

indicators.note: change here is the call to mix up the letters once the swap is made
for signals one letter standing in place of another
touch of takes only the opening letter of embarrassment

explanation.surface: An angler awkwardly means amplification, to their embarrassment, as a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touch of embarrassment for a' swaps E in for one A of ANGLERMEANT; 'change' then rearranges ENGLERMEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An enlargement makes something bigger, just as amplification increases size or volume.

clue.text: Rugby team not beginning well, all-in after scrum

indicators.note: after a scrum the forwards end up jumbled, so these letters are mixed up
not beginning tells you to drop the opening letter of well

explanation.surface: A rugby side is out of form and exhausted after a scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not beginning' gives ELL; with ALL-IN that is rearranged by 'after scrum', the scrum being a rugby set piece where players pile in.
explanation.definitionFit: Llanelli is a town in south Wales famous for its rugby union club.

clue.text: See 1
Stack up records about unknown disease

indicators.note: about has the records word wrapped round the stack word

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
to stack up is to pile things
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Piling up the records about an unknown illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stack up' is the phrasal verb pile up, not a reversal; 'about' wraps the records round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder causing seizures, so it is an illness.

clue.text: String theory

definitions.meaning: catgut is used for the strings of instruments and racquets
The abbreviation for Grand Unified Theory in physics

explanation.surface: The physics idea of string theory.
explanation.definitionFit: Catgut makes strings, and physicists shorten Grand Unified Theory to its initials.

clue.text: Old Iranian artefact ultimately given to me

parts.note: Median is the language of the ancient Medes of Iran

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of artefact

explanation.surface: An ancient Persian relic is finally handed over to me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the third note of the tonic sol-fa scale, and the mediant is the third degree of a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: In sol-fa, me (mi) is the third note, the degree musicians call the mediant.

clue.text: One over the moon over a girl?

indicators.note: over in a down clue turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: the LEM, lunar excursion module, flew over the moon

explanation.surface: Someone delighted about a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the moon' suggests delight; it is literal here: the Apollo lunar module, LEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mel is a female name, short for Melanie.

clue.text: Recorder heard in appalling joint

indicators.note: heard tells you the words are said aloud and sound like the answer

parts.note: appalling is dire and a joint is the wrist

explanation.surface: A tape recorder caught in a dreadful dive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a seedy venue; it is the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A diarist keeps a daily journal, so they record events.

clue.text: Cork particle found in marine creature

parts.note: to cork a bottle is to seal it
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A bit of cork found inside a sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cork' looks like the Irish city or the material; it is a verb meaning SEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea lion is an eared seal that lives in the ocean.

clue.text: Waste no opportunity to reverse every Roller?

definitions.meaning: to flip over each rolling stone, as in the proverb about gathering no moss

explanation.surface: Make the most of every chance to turn a Rolls-Royce round.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means searching exhaustively, and literally it describes turning over every rock that rolls.

clue.text: Sue's a dish, footloose and aspirational at heart

indicators.note: footloose means losing the foot, the bottom letter in a down clue

parts.note: an entree is a dish served at a meal

indicators.note: at heart takes the central letters of aspirational

explanation.surface: Sue is gorgeous, carefree and ambitious underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a name; it is the verb. 'footloose' drops the last E of ENTREE; the middle of ASPIRATIONAL is AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue for something is to plead or beg, as in sue for peace.

clue.text: Pianist in tour oddly forgetting where he's supposed to be?

indicators.note: oddly forgetting means dropping the first, third, fifth letters and so on, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A touring pianist who keeps forgetting where he is meant to be.
explanation.definitionFit: In situ is Latin for in its original or proper place.

clue.text: TV personality acquiring name as composer

parts.note: tele is short for television
a man is a person, here a television personality

explanation.surface: A TV star picks up a name as a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: TELEMAN, a TV man, gains N (name).
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Philipp Telemann was a prolific German Baroque composer.

clue.text: Chatted when rung

definitions.meaning: a rod of a wheel or a step of a ladder

explanation.surface: Talked when telephoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Talked is the past of speak, and a wheel's radial bar or a ladder rung is also one.

clue.text: "Tree" (sing.) initially in Latin is rendered neuter

indicators.note: rendered means translated or made into something else, so these letters are reformed
initially takes the opening letters of sing, in and Latin

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry translating the Latin singular word for tree as neuter.
explanation.walkthrough: TREE, S I L and IS rearranged by 'rendered' give the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To neuter an animal is to make it unable to breed, the same as to sterilise it.

clue.text: Larwood regularly left — not at Trent Bridge when required?

definitions.text: not at Trent Bridge when required?

indicators.note: regularly takes every second letter of Larwood

explanation.surface: Harold Larwood often left, missing from Trent Bridge when needed.
explanation.walkthrough: Trent Bridge is the Nottingham cricket ground, and Harold Larwood was a Nottinghamshire fast bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent without leave describes someone missing from duty, as a player missing from his ground.

clue.text: Mrs von Trapp shortly to turn up -that's a gas!

indicators.note: to turn up in a down clue means reading the letters upward, from bottom to top
shortly cuts the name down by dropping its opening pair

parts.note: Maria von Trapp, the Sound of Music heroine, became Mrs von Trapp

explanation.surface: Mrs von Trapp is about to arrive: what fun!
explanation.walkthrough: MARIA cut short to RIA, then 'to turn up' reverses it. 'a gas' looks like slang for fun; it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Air is the mixture of gases we breathe, so it is a gas.
